promptHtml: Put Vivado's steps in order, from your files to a configured chip.
explanationHtml: Each step needs the one before it. Synthesis decides which cells the code needs; place and route decides where each one goes and how they connect; the bitstream records all of that in one file; programming loads the file into the chip.
steps: Write the design and its constraints file.
Synthesis turns the code into cells, such as LUTs and pin buffers.
Place and route gives each cell a place on the chip and wires them together.
Programming loads the bitstream into the FPGA.

promptHtml: Vivado built vote.sv for the Arty A7-100T. Below is the Primitives table of its Utilization report: one row for each kind of cell, with how many the design uses.
explanationHtml: An input buffer, IBUF, joins one input pin to the logic inside the chip, so synthesis adds one for each input port. vote has three inputs, a, b and c, and the IBUF row matches them. Its one output, y, has its own OBUF, and the LUT3 row is the LUT of lesson 0.1.
ask: How many input buffers did synthesis add for vote's input pins?

promptHtml: This part of vote's Utilization report is about the FPGA's pins. A bonded IOB (input/output block) is the circuit behind one of the chip's pins: "bonded" means joined to a pin of its package. Used counts the pins this design uses. Fixed counts those whose place the constraints file gave, instead of Vivado choosing it.
explanationHtml: vote.xdc has one PACKAGE_PIN line for each of vote's four ports, a, b, c and y, so every pin vote uses is fixed, and the Used and Fixed columns agree. Vivado still chose where the LUT3 went, but not the pins: the board wires its switches and LEDs to particular pins, and only the constraints file says which.
excerpt: |          Site Type          | Used | Fixed | Prohibited | Available | Util% |
ask: How many of vote's pins did its constraints file fix?

promptHtml: These are the first lines of vote's Utilization report: which design it is about, which chip, and which step of the build Vivado had finished when it wrote the report.
explanationHtml: The Design State line names the last step finished before the report was written: here routing, the second half of place and route. So these counts are the cells actually placed on the chip. Vivado also writes a report straight after synthesis, whose Design State line names synthesis instead.
ask: What does the report's Design State line say?

promptHtml: You want vote's output on LED LD5 instead of LD4. What do you change?
explanationHtml: The code never names pins: only the constraints file ties each port to a pin. So you give y's PACKAGE_PIN line the pin the board wires to LD5, and build again. A port's name and its place in the list say nothing about pins, and Vivado does not know what the board wires to each pin until the constraints file tells it.
options: The name of the port `y` in `vote.sv`.
The order of the ports in `vote.sv`.
Nothing: Vivado moves `y` to a free LED when it builds again.

promptHtml: Put in order what happens to vote's one assign line on its way to the board, from the code to a lit LED.
explanationHtml: Synthesis decides what the line becomes: one LUT3 whose eight bits are vote's truth table (lesson 0.1). Placement then picks which of the chip's LUTs will hold them, and routing connects it to the pins that vote.xdc names (lesson 0.3). The bitstream carries the bits and the connections, and the LUT only holds its bits, and so only computes y, once the chip has loaded that file (lesson 0.1).
steps: The line is turned into eight bits, one for each row of a truth table.
One of the FPGA's many LUTs is chosen to hold those bits.
Connections are chosen from that LUT to the pins wired to SW0, SW1, SW2 and LD4.
The eight bits and every chosen connection are written into one file.
The chip loads the file: the LUT now holds the bits, and any two of SW0, SW1 and SW2 set to 1 light LD4.
